subject: english-language
title: From Lakoff to Cameron
welcome_lead: Trace the arc from deficit to performance — three decades of theorising the link between language and gender.
meta_desc: Lakoff, Zimmerman & West, Tannen, Cameron — the major frameworks at A-Level English Language.
final_note: You have toured the historiography of language and gender — each model corrects the last while leaving useful tools.

concepts.def: Robin Lakoff (1975) — women's language shows features of powerlessness.
Zimmerman & West (1975) — mixed-sex talk reflects male dominance through interruptions.
Deborah Tannen (1990) — men and women belong to different sub-cultures.
Butler / Cameron — gender is produced through talk; differences are exaggerated.
O'Barr & Atkins (1980) — Lakoff's features index status, not sex.
Crenshaw — gender intersects with race, class, age and sexuality.

walkthroughs.h2: Four Frameworks in a Sentence Each
walkthroughs.body_html:
Deficit: women's talk is deficient. Dominance: male talk dominates. Difference: men and women are differently socialised. Performative: gender is done in talk.

Knowing the order and the key thinker for each is the spine of an A-Level answer.

Dominance answered Lakoff's biological essentialism by re-framing features as power-driven. Tannen answered dominance by foregrounding cultural learning. Cameron answered difference by showing the alleged gaps were tiny.
In an A-Level data response, apply more than one model. Show how Lakoff's features could be re-described as power (O'Barr) or as performative stance (Butler).
